messages.subject: code issue :(
parts:
Hi, I'm having problem with a code to create a new dataset...here's the code:

SumStats<-ddply(total_svo,c("condition"),summarise,
 N=length(SVO),
 mean=mean(SVO),
 sd=sd(SOV),
 se=sd/sqrt(N)
 )

And that's the error that always comes out: "Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'N' not found".
In your opinion, whhhhyyy is it? Thanks in advance for your help :)

Sara

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: code issue :(
parts:
Well, probably as the error stated, you have not defined N (inside the function call doesn’t count). try replacing sqrt(N) with sqrt(length(SVO)).

Note that this is not a Deducer related query. Please redirect future questions like this to stackoverflow or r-help.

Best,
Ian

messages.author: 056a0f54645c6009
messages.subject: Remove legend from plots
parts:
Hi all,

Working on creating plots and then once parameters are set I will try to
create a template for use for all of the necessary plots.

I have been doing a lot of Trial & Error with the Legend section of
Theme in Plot Builder but can not eliminate the legend. I can remove
the text, rectangles and virtually everything but the points remain on
the right (default). Both the X - Y Axes have the necessary
information, therefore the legend is redundant. So I would like to
remove it.

Clearly I am missing something basic here.

Cheers,

Bruce

messages.author: 30dc0c001c553eb0
messages.subject: Re: code issue :(
parts:
One way of removing the legend would be 
    Deducer Plot Builder - Templates - Scales - from there select colour identity or what else may apply - then go to Legend and switch to none
